stem:
Imran sends several torch rays that are parallel to one another onto the same plane mirror shown below.

What happens to those rays after reflection?

options.text: They must meet at a point behind the mirror, because that is what every mirror does.
They stay parallel to one another after reflection from the flat sheet.
They spread apart as if the sheet were a convex surface, even though the sheet is flat.
Only the hatch marks on the back of the mirror decide whether the rays meet.

teacher.key_rationale: A plane mirror keeps a bundle of parallel rays parallel. Meeting at a point is a concave-mirror story, not this flat sheet.
teacher.figure_note: Same plane-mirror tikzpicture as 0625_m19_qp_12:q22, used as the flat sheet.
